instructions: Credentials are placeholders, never real secrets. Never ask the user for a real secret. Prefer vault_http for API calls; use vault_get_placeholder only for tools that must run natively. Put a placeholder only where the usage field says. A placeholder anywhere else is refused. On AV_PH_EXHAUSTED or AV_PH_STALE, call vault_get_placeholder again and retry. On a denial, call vault_explain_denial with the request_id to learn the rule and the allowed alternatives. Before a write you are unsure of, call vault_preflight; to learn your limits, call vault_describe_access.

tools.name: vault_status
tools.description: Whether the vault is reachable and unlocked, and a summary of the current session.

tools.name: vault_list_creds
tools.description: Credentials this session may use, with the exact place a placeholder goes for each.

tools.name: vault_get_placeholder
tools.description: Get a placeholder for a credential. Returns the placeholder plus where to put it.

reason.description: why you need it; shown to the human as an unverified claim

uses.description: optional: make it n-use instead of session-lifetime

tools.name: vault_request_session
tools.description: Ask a human for a session. This creates nothing by itself: it opens a request a human must approve, and they may narrow it first. Poll the returned id until they answer. Two error paths already tell you to call this.

reason.description: why you need it; shown to the human as an unverified claim

methods.description: ask for the least you need

ttl_minutes.description: how long you need it for; ask for the least you need

uses.description: optional: n-use placeholders instead of session-lifetime ones

grant_ttl_minutes.description: how long the access itself is needed, if shorter than the session

routes.description: optional: method-bound routes, each a set of methods allowed only on these paths

template.description: a template name the human saved; they see the template, not a policy to read

poll_id.description: an id from an earlier call: check whether it has been answered

poll_secret.description: the poll_secret that earlier call returned; only the asker can poll

tools.name: vault_approval_status
tools.description: Whether a human has answered a held request. The 202 from a held write names this tool and the id to pass.

tools.name: vault_http
tools.description: Make an HTTP request through the vault. The credential is injected by the daemon; you never handle it.

tools.name: vault_explain_denial
tools.description: Explain why a request this session made was denied and what this session is allowed to do instead. The code and rule are always given; the full sentence is kept for an hour (the last 1000 denials) and is null after that, after the daemon restarts, or for a caller with no session.

tools.name: vault_describe_access
tools.description: What this session may do right now: hosts, methods, paths, approval mode, budgets and limits, lifetimes, and where each placeholder goes.

tools.name: vault_preflight
tools.description: Check whether a request would be allowed, held for a human, or refused, without sending it or spending anything. Advisory only.

path.description: the upstream path, as for vault_http
